source: slskd 0.22.5 DownloadService.cs (the terminal catch in the download task, which overwrites the library's disposition) + Soulseek.NET 7.0.3 TransferStates.cs, read at the tag; every terminal state additionally witnessed by a fixture recorded from a running instance of this version
note: The transfer states the PINNED slskd can put on a download row. Soulseek.NET defines more flags than this, but slskd 0.22.5's own catch rewrites the terminal record — OperationCanceledException to Completed|Cancelled, everything else to Completed|Errored — so the library's Rejected/TimedOut/Aborted dispositions never survive to the API. Failure differentiation therefore lives entirely in the `exception` text, not in the state. A unit stub naming a state outside `reachable` is testing a provider that does not exist; the vocabulary test enforces that. This record is version-scoped on purpose: bumping slskd (0.26 makes TimedOut terminal, starts downloads as `Queued, Locally`, and lets a failed transfer return to queued) must mean re-recording and rewriting this file, not editing a stub until it passes.

reachable.Requested: asked of the peer, no answer yet
reachable.Queued, Locally: momentary, before the peer is asked
reachable.Queued, Remotely: the peer deferred us into its queue
reachable.Initializing: the peer accepted and the connection is coming up
reachable.Completed, Errored: everything else that went wrong, whatever the cause

unreachable.Completed, Rejected: Soulseek.NET raises it, slskd 0.22.5 overwrites it with Completed|Errored before the API can serve it — the peer's refusal survives only as the exception text 'Transfer rejected: …'
unreachable.Completed, TimedOut: same overwrite; a timeout reaches us as Completed|Errored with 'timed out' in the exception. Becomes genuinely terminal in slskd 0.26
unreachable.Completed, Aborted: same overwrite; raised for a size mismatch
